Advanced Energy Launches Ultra-Ruggedized 160 W AC-DC Power Supply for Extreme Environments
The Defiant Future family is designed to deliver uninterrupted power to critical applications where reliability is non-negotiable.
DF150 is the first model in the new Defiant Future family of commercial defense power supplies certified to meet MIL-STD 810H and MIL-STD 461G standards
DENVER, September 24, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Advanced Energy Industries Inc. (Nasdaq: AEIS), a global leader in highly engineered, precision power conversion, measurement and control solutions, today launches the ruggedized DF150 160 W AC-DC power supply. This is the first offering in the company's Defiant Future (DF) series of robust, high-reliability standard power supplies for extreme-environment applications across the defense, industrial, telecommunications, transportation and energy sectors.
Backed by rigorous validation testing, the DF150 power supply features a broad spectrum of MIL-STD certifications, combining proven performance with the shorter lead times of a standard power supply. It is certified to MIL-STD 810H, withstanding harsh conditions including shock, vibration, altitude variations and thermal extremes. DF150 also provides enhanced electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) performance with certification to MIL-STD 461G. The unit delivers a nominal 27 VDC at 6 A (160 W) with no performance degradation across its extended operating temperature range of -46ºC to +60ºC. With its IP67 rating, DF150 is fully submersible and exceeds MIL-STD ingress protection requirements for dust and liquids.
"The Defiant Future family is designed to deliver uninterrupted power to critical applications where reliability is non-negotiable," said Joe Voyles, Advanced Energy's vice president, Industrial Power Conversion Products. "The DF150 marks a significant step forward in what is possible from a standard commercial defense power supply. It delivers the performance and breadth of MIL-STD certifications often associated with custom-designed solutions with the availability and lead-time advantages of a standard commercial product."
The DF150 delivers up to 91% efficiency at full load. It operates with no minimum load and low leakage (275 µA at 230 VAC). Its MIL-STD-461G certification includes RE102, CE102, CS101, CS114, CS115, CS116, CS118 and RS103. Advanced Energy offers the DF150 with conduction cooling via a base plate or convection cooling with a mounted heatsink. Other options include various input cable configurations and case colors. Learn more about the DF150 and Defiant Future family.
Advanced Energy (Nasdaq: AEIS) is a global leader in the design and manufacturing of highly engineered, precision power conversion, measurement and control solutions for applications and processes. AE's power solutions enable customer innovation in complex applications for a wide range of industries including semiconductor equipment, industrial, manufacturing, telecommunications, data center computing and healthcare. With engineering know-how and responsive service and support around the globe, the company builds collaborative partnerships to meet technology advances, propel growth for its customers and innovate the future of power. Advanced Energy has devoted four decades to perfecting power for its global customers and is headquartered in Denver, Colorado, USA.
For more information, visit www.advancedenergy.com.

3 Reasons to Avoid AGYS and 1 Stock to Buy Instead
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 10:33 AM PDT 3 min read
3 Reasons to Avoid AGYS and 1 Stock to Buy Instead
Agilysys has had an impressive run over the past six months as its shares have beaten the S&P 500 by 12.7%. The stock now trades at $96.31, marking a 33.8% gain. This was partly thanks to its solid quarterly results, and the run-up might have investors contemplating their next move.
Is there a buying opportunity in Agilysys, or does it present a risk to your portfolio? Get the full breakdown from our expert analysts, it's free.
Why Is Agilysys Not Exciting?
We're happy investors have made money, but we don't have much confidence in Agilysys. Here are three reasons we avoid AGYS, plus one stock we'd rather own.
1. Low Gross Margin Reveals Weak Structural Profitability
For software companies like Agilysys, gross profit tells us how much money remains after paying for the base cost of products and services (typically servers, licenses, and certain personnel). These costs are usually low as a percentage of revenue, explaining why software is more lucrative than other sectors.

Advanced Energy Launches Ultra-Ruggedized 160 W AC-DC Power Supply for Extreme Environments
The Defiant Future family is designed to deliver uninterrupted power to critical applications where reliability is non-negotiable.
DF150 is the first model in the new Defiant Future family of commercial defense power supplies certified to meet MIL-STD 810H and MIL-STD 461G standards
DENVER, September 24, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Advanced Energy Industries Inc. (Nasdaq: AEIS), a global leader in highly engineered, precision power conversion, measurement and control solutions, today launches the ruggedized DF150 160 W AC-DC power supply. This is the first offering in the company's Defiant Future (DF) series of robust, high-reliability standard power supplies for extreme-environment applications across the defense, industrial, telecommunications, transportation and energy sectors.
Backed by rigorous validation testing, the DF150 power supply features a broad spectrum of MIL-STD certifications, combining proven performance with the shorter lead times of a standard power supply. It is certified to MIL-STD 810H, withstanding harsh conditions including shock, vibration, altitude variations and thermal extremes. DF150 also provides enhanced electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) performance with certification to MIL-STD 461G. The unit delivers a nominal 27 VDC at 6 A (160 W) with no performance degradation across its extended operating temperature range of -46ºC to +60ºC. With its IP67 rating, DF150 is fully submersible and exceeds MIL-STD ingress protection requirements for dust and liquids.
"The Defiant Future family is designed to deliver uninterrupted power to critical applications where reliability is non-negotiable," said Joe Voyles, Advanced Energy's vice president, Industrial Power Conversion Products. "The DF150 marks a significant step forward in what is possible from a standard commercial defense power supply. It delivers the performance and breadth of MIL-STD certifications often associated with custom-designed solutions with the availability and lead-time advantages of a standard commercial product."
The DF150 delivers up to 91% efficiency at full load. It operates with no minimum load and low leakage (275 µA at 230 VAC). Its MIL-STD-461G certification includes RE102, CE102, CS101, CS114, CS115, CS116, CS118 and RS103. Advanced Energy offers the DF150 with conduction cooling via a base plate or convection cooling with a mounted heatsink. Other options include various input cable configurations and case colors. Learn more about the DF150 and Defiant Future family.
Advanced Energy (Nasdaq: AEIS) is a global leader in the design and manufacturing of highly engineered, precision power conversion, measurement and control solutions for applications and processes. AE's power solutions enable customer innovation in complex applications for a wide range of industries including semiconductor equipment, industrial, manufacturing, telecommunications, data center computing and healthcare. With engineering know-how and responsive service and support around the globe, the company builds collaborative partnerships to meet technology advances, propel growth for its customers and innovate the future of power. Advanced Energy has devoted four decades to perfecting power for its global customers and is headquartered in Denver, Colorado, USA.
For more information, visit www.advancedenergy.com.

(Nasdaq: AEIS), a global leader in highly engineered, precision power conversion, measurement and control solutions, today launches the ruggedized DF150 160 W AC-DC power supply. This is the first offering in the company's Defiant Future (DF) series of robust, high-reliability standard power supplies for extreme-environment applications across the defense, industrial, telecommunications, transportation and energy sectors.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260924025432/en/
The Defiant Future family is designed to deliver uninterrupted power to critical applications where reliability is non-negotiable.
Backed by rigorous validation testing, the DF150 power supply features a broad spectrum of MIL-STD certifications, combining proven performance with the shorter lead times of a standard power supply. It s certified to MIL-STD 810H, withstanding harsh conditions including shock, vibration, altitude variations and thermal extremes. DF150 also provides enhanced electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) performance with certification to MIL-STD 461G. The unit delivers a nominal 27 VDC at 6 A (160 W) with no performance degradation across its extended operating temperature range of -46ºC to +60ºC. With its IP67 rating, DF150 is fully submersible and exceeds MIL-STD ingress protection requirements for dust and liquids.
"The Defiant Future family is designed to deliver uninterrupted power to critical applications where reliability is non-negotiable," said Joe Voyles, Advanced Energy's vice president, Industrial Power Conversion Products. "The DF150 marks a significant step forward in what is possible from a standard commercial defense power supply. It delivers the performance and breadth of MIL-STD certifications often associated with custom-designed solutions with the availability and lead-time advantages of a standard commercial product."
The DF150 delivers up to 91% efficiency at full load. It operates with no minimum load and low leakage (275 µA at 230 VAC). Its MIL-STD-461G certification includes RE102, CE102, CS101, CS114, CS115, CS116, CS118 and RS103. Advanced Energy offers the DF150 with conduction cooling via a base plate or convection cooling with a mounted heatsink. Other options include various input cable configurations and case colors. Learn more about the DF150 and Defiant Future family.
Advanced Energy (Nasdaq: AEIS) is a global leader in the design and manufacturing of highly engineered, precision power conversion, measurement and control solutions for applications and processes. AE's power solutions enable customer innovation in complex applications for a wide range of industries including semiconductor equipment, industrial, manufacturing, telecommunications, data center computing and healthcare. With engineering know-how and responsive service and support around the globe, the company builds collaborative partnerships to meet technology advances, propel growth for its customers and innovate the future of power. Advanced Energy has devoted four decades to perfecting power for its global customers and is headquartered in Denver, Colorado, USA.
For more information, visit www.advancedenergy.com.

3 Reasons to Avoid AGYS and 1 Stock to Buy Instead
Agilysys has had an impressive run over the past six months as its shares have beaten the S&P 500 by 12.7%. The stock now trades at $96.31, marking a 33.8% gain. This was partly thanks to its solid quarterly results, and the run-up might have investors contemplating their next move.
Is there a buying opportunity in Agilysys, or does it present a risk to your portfolio? Get the full breakdown from our expert analysts, it's free.
Why Is Agilysys Not Exciting?
We're happy investors have made money, but we don't have much confidence in Agilysys. Here are three reasons we avoid AGYS, plus one stock we'd rather own.
1. Low Gross Margin Reveals Weak Structural Profitability
For software companies like Agilysys, gross profit tells us how much money remains after paying for the base cost of products and services (typically servers, licenses, and certain personnel). These costs are usually low as a percentage of revenue, explaining why software is more lucrative than other sectors.
Agilysys's gross margin is substantially worse than most software businesses, signaling it has relatively high infrastructure costs compared to asset-lite businesses like ServiceNow. As you can see below, it averaged a 63.1% gross margin over the last year. That means Agilysys paid its providers a lot of money ($36.94 for every $100 in revenue) to run its business.
The market not only cares about gross margin levels but also how they change over time because expansion creates firepower for profitability and free cash generation. Agilysys has seen gross margins improve by 1.4 percentage points over the last 2 years, which is solid in the software space.
While many software businesses point investors to their adjusted profits, which exclude stock-based compensation (SBC), we prefer GAAP operating margin because SBC is a legitimate expense used to attract and retain talent. This metric shows how much revenue remains after accounting for all core expenses — everything from the cost of goods sold to sales and R&D.
Analyzing the trend in its profitability, Agilysys's operating margin rose by 7.2 percentage points over the last two years, as its sales growth gave it operating leverage. Its operating margin for the trailing 12 months was 14.6%.
Agilysys Trailing 12-Month Operating Margin (GAAP)
If you've followed StockStory for a while, you know we emphasize free cash flow. Why, you ask? We believe that in the end, cash is king, and you can't use accounting profits to pay the bills.
Over the next year, analysts predict Agilysys's cash conversion will fall. Their consensus estimates imply its free cash flow margin of 24.4% for the last 12 months will decrease to 21.3%.
Agilysys isn't a terrible business, but it doesn't pass our bar. With its shares beating the market recently, the stock trades at 7.1× forward price-to-sales (or $96.31 per share). Agilysys, Inc. And 7 Cedars Resort Properties Expand Use Of Agilysys Ecosystem To Streamline Gaming Operations, Reduce Manual Processes And Improve Staff Efficiency
AGILYSYS, INC.
Agilysys, Inc. announced the expansion of its relationship with 7 Cedars Resort Properties. The Agilysys ecosystem will be supporting hotel, gaming, golf, retail, and food and beverage operations at 7 Cedars. The software solutions installed recently include Agilysys Versa property management system and the modernized version of Agilysys InfoGenesis point of sale, along with several other hardware and software solutions.
After researching several well-known technology solution providers, 7 Cedars ultimately chose Agilysys due to its integration capabilities, cost-effectiveness, and suitability for their complex casino environment. Opened in 2020, the 7 Cedars Hotel and Casino is located along the Salish Coast 60 miles north of Seattle. The property also offers a golf course, six food and beverage outlets and five banquet spaces all supported by Agilysys software solutions.
Since expanding its partnership with Agilysys, 7 Cedars has seen a dramatic improvement in staff productivity across all departments, automating several manual processes. In addition, the property has seen an impressive jump in reservations and revenue increases across all channels. While Agilysys Versa PMS centralizes all operations, 7 Cedars also chose Versa for its reporting and database management features.
Converting to the modernized version of Agilysys InfoGenesis point-of-sale POS system allowed users to change screen layouts a lot easier and search for food and retail items much faster. Agilysys Book was selected to increase direct bookings, reduce OTA commissions and unify multi-amenity reservations by combining hotel and casino guests into a single seamless transaction. Additional solutions implemented recently at 7 Cedars include Agilysys Express Mobile for self-service mobile check-in; Agilysys Sales & Catering to improve efficiencies in the management of events, meetings and group services across all outlets; DataMagine document management system to securely digitize and centralize hotel, resort and casino registrations and payments; and Agilysys Digital Marketing for centralized control over guest communications to increase direct bookings, reduce acquisition costs, drive guest revenue and improve marketing efficiency through intelligent use of guest profiles across the Agilysys ecosystem.

3 Reasons to Avoid AGYS and 1 Stock to Buy Instead
Agilysys has had an impressive run over the past six months as its shares have beaten the S&P 500 by 12.7%. The stock now trades at $96.31, marking a 33.8% gain. This was partly thanks to its solid quarterly results, and the run-up might have investors contemplating their next move.
Is there a buying opportunity in Agilysys, or does it present a risk to your portfolio? Get the full breakdown from our expert analysts, it's free.
Why Is Agilysys Not Exciting?
We're happy investors have made money, but we don't have much confidence in Agilysys. Here are three reasons we avoid AGYS, plus one stock we'd rather own.
1. Low Gross Margin Reveals Weak Structural Profitability
For software companies like Agilysys, gross profit tells us how much money remains after paying for the base cost of products and services (typically servers, licenses, and certain personnel). These costs are usually low as a percentage of revenue, explaining why software is more lucrative than other sectors.
Agilysys's gross margin is substantially worse than most software businesses, signaling it has relatively high infrastructure costs compared to asset-lite businesses like ServiceNow. As you can see below, it averaged a 63.1% gross margin over the last year. That means Agilysys paid its providers a lot of money ($36.94 for every $100 in revenue) to run its business.
The market not only cares about gross margin levels but also how they change over time because expansion creates firepower for profitability and free cash generation. Agilysys has seen gross margins improve by 1.4 percentage points over the last 2 years, which is solid in the software space.
While many software businesses point investors to their adjusted profits, which exclude stock-based compensation (SBC), we prefer GAAP operating margin because SBC is a legitimate expense used to attract and retain talent. This metric shows how much revenue remains after accounting for all core expenses — everything from the cost of goods sold to sales and R&D.
Analyzing the trend in its profitability, Agilysys's operating margin rose by 7.2 percentage points over the last two years, as its sales growth gave it operating leverage. Its operating margin for the trailing 12 months was 14.6%.
Agilysys Trailing 12-Month Operating Margin (GAAP)
If you've followed StockStory for a while, you know we emphasize free cash flow. Why, you ask? We believe that in the end, cash is king, and you can't use accounting profits to pay the bills.
Over the next year, analysts predict Agilysys's cash conversion will fall. Their consensus estimates imply its free cash flow margin of 24.4% for the last 12 months will decrease to 21.3%.
Agilysys isn't a terrible business, but it doesn't pass our bar. With its shares beating the market recently, the stock trades at 7.1× forward price-to-sales (or $96.31 per share). While this valuation is reasonable, we don't really see a big opportunity at the moment. We're fairly confident there are better investments elsewhere. Agilysys, Inc. And 7 Cedars Resort Properties Expand Use Of Agilysys Ecosystem To Streamline Gaming Operations, Reduce Manual Processes And Improve Staff Efficiency
AGILYSYS, INC.
Agilysys, Inc. announced the expansion of its relationship with 7 Cedars Resort Properties. The Agilysys ecosystem will be supporting hotel, gaming, golf, retail, and food and beverage operations at 7 Cedars. The software solutions installed recently include Agilysys Versa property management system and the modernized version of Agilysys InfoGenesis point of sale, along with several other hardware and software solutions.
After researching several well-known technology solution providers, 7 Cedars ultimately chose Agilysys due to its integration capabilities, cost-effectiveness, and suitability for their complex casino environment. Opened in 2020, the 7 Cedars Hotel and Casino is located along the Salish Coast 60 miles north of Seattle. The property also offers a golf course, six food and beverage outlets and five banquet spaces all supported by Agilysys software solutions.
Since expanding its partnership with Agilysys, 7 Cedars has seen a dramatic improvement in staff productivity across all departments, automating several manual processes. In addition, the property has seen an impressive jump in reservations and revenue increases across all channels. While Agilysys Versa PMS centralizes all operations, 7 Cedars also chose Versa for its reporting and database management features.
Converting to the modernized version of Agilysys InfoGenesis point-of-sale POS system allowed users to change screen layouts a lot easier and search for food and retail items much faster. Agilysys Book was selected to increase direct bookings, reduce OTA commissions and unify multi-amenity reservations by combining hotel and casino guests into a single seamless transaction. Additional solutions implemented recently at 7 Cedars include Agilysys Express Mobile for self-service mobile check-in; Agilysys Sales & Catering to improve efficiencies in the management of events, meetings and group services across all outlets; DataMagine document management system to securely digitize and centralize hotel, resort and casino registrations and payments; and Agilysys Digital Marketing for centralized control over guest communications to increase direct bookings, reduce acquisition costs, drive guest revenue and improve marketing efficiency through intelligent use of guest profiles across the Agilysys ecosystem.
